lines: @@ -13,6 +13,23 @@ This page only lists breaking and critical changes that affect self-hosted Opik
If you are upgrading from Opik 1.x to Opik 2.x, follow the [Opik 2.0 migration guide](/self-host/v1-to-v2-migration).
+The Python code executor that runs code metrics now sandboxes user code by default:

+- `PYTHON_CODE_EXECUTOR_PROCESS_NETWORK_ISOLATION` (`process` strategy, the default) now defaults to `true`. Each worker runs as an unprivileged user with a minimal environment and no network access.

+- `PYTHON_CODE_EXECUTOR_DOCKER_HARDENING` (`docker` strategy) now defaults to `true`. Executor containers run with no capabilities, a read-only root filesystem, a small `noexec` `/tmp` and a process limit.
+Docker Compose and Helm deployments that keep the default python-backend settings need no change: python-backend runs as root, which process isolation requires.
+Set either one back to `false` (in the Helm chart under `component.python-backend.env`, or as an environment variable for Docker Compose) when:

+- **python-backend runs as non-root with the `process` strategy.** Isolation can't be applied there, so no process worker starts and every code metric evaluation fails. The python-backend log names `PYTHON_CODE_EXECUTOR_PROCESS_NETWORK_ISOLATION` and the step that failed. Set it to `false`.

+- **Code metrics open network connections or read environment variables under the `process` strategy.** Isolated workers can't create sockets and see only a minimal environment, so such a metric now fails. Set `PYTHON_CODE_EXECUTOR_PROCESS_NETWORK_ISOLATION` to `false`.

+- **Code metrics write outside `/tmp`, write more than 16 MB to `/tmp`, or start more than 64 processes or threads under the `docker` strategy.** Set `PYTHON_CODE_EXECUTOR_DOCKER_HARDENING` to `false`, or raise `PYTHON_CODE_EXECUTOR_DOCKER_TMPFS_SIZE` and `PYTHON_CODE_EXECUTOR_DOCKER_PIDS_LIMIT`.

- `PYTHON_CODE_EXECUTOR_ALLOW_NETWORK`: set to `true` to allow network access in executor containers (default: false)

Workers fork from a minimal template process started at startup, before any per-request state and with only an allowlisted environment, so user code does not start from the backend's memory or inherit its environment. The template loads only the light metric interface; a metric that uses more of `opik` loads the rest on first use. Needs Linux, Python 3.14 (as in the python-backend image; on another version no worker starts and the error names the version) and the python-backend container running as root with CAP_SETUID/CAP_SETGID (granted to root by default; no privileged mode or extra capability), and works under a container seccomp profile such as RuntimeDefault. If isolation can't be applied no worker starts and an error naming this setting and the failed step is logged. Any value other than `true` or `false` fails startup

- `PYTHON_CODE_EXECUTOR_MAX_RESULT_SIZE_IN_BYTES`: largest result a `process` strategy worker may return, as JSON; a longer result fails that evaluation. A positive integer; any other value fails `process` strategy startup (default: 67108864, i.e. 64 MiB)

- `PYTHON_CODE_EXECUTOR_READY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`: how long a new `process` strategy worker may take to start and report ready; a worker that takes longer is stopped and not added to the pool. A positive number of seconds; any other value fails `process` strategy startup (default: 10)
- `PYTHON_CODE_EXECUTOR_CPU_SHARES`: Docker CPU shares for containers, higher = higher priority (default: 512, Docker default is 1024)
- `PYTHON_CODE_EXECUTOR_MEM_LIMIT`: Memory limit for executor containers, uses Docker format with single letter unit b/k/m/g (default: 256m)
- `PYTHON_CODE_EXECUTOR_CPU_LIMIT`: Hard CPU limit per executor container in fractional CPUs, e.g. "0.5" = half a core (default: unset, no hard limit)

-  - `PYTHON_CODE_EXECUTOR_DOCKER_HARDENING`: `docker` strategy only. Set to `true` to start executor containers with all capabilities dropped, a read-only root filesystem with a small `noexec` `/tmp` and a process limit, and, while `PYTHON_CODE_EXECUTOR_ALLOW_NETWORK` is `false`, to run the in-container Docker daemon without a bridge network or iptables rules (default: false). Metrics that write outside `/tmp` or start many processes fail. Any value other than `true` or `false` fails startup

+  - `PYTHON_CODE_EXECUTOR_DOCKER_HARDENING`: `docker` strategy only. When `true`, starts executor containers with all capabilities dropped, a read-only root filesystem with a small `noexec` `/tmp` and a process limit, and, while `PYTHON_CODE_EXECUTOR_ALLOW_NETWORK` is `false`, runs the in-container Docker daemon without a bridge network or iptables rules (default: true). Metrics that write outside `/tmp` or start many processes fail; set it to `false` for them. Any value other than `true` or `false` fails startup
- `PYTHON_CODE_EXECUTOR_DOCKER_PIDS_LIMIT`: process limit per executor container when hardening is on. A positive integer (default: 64)
- `PYTHON_CODE_EXECUTOR_DOCKER_TMPFS_SIZE`: size of the writable `/tmp` per executor container when hardening is on, e.g. `16m` (default: 16m)
- `PYTHON_CODE_EXECUTOR_METRICS_INTERVAL_IN_SECONDS`: Interval for collecting executor container CPU/memory metrics via Docker stats API (default: 60)
